title: St. Francis of Assisi's stigmata as UFO radiation

tellings.quote: Just take the case of Saint Francis of Assisi. His close confidant, Brother Leo, documents the experience describing and fury, creating atmospheric sparks, a spinning disk, telepathic communication between Francis and the disc.
the best report shows that brother Leo who's about 15 he's watching and he sees that this is how he describes it that this thing dealt harshly with Francis afterwards Francis was injured

as_told.title: St. Francis's stigmata as electromagnetic damage

plain: Saint Francis of Assisi's famous vision on Mount La Verna in Italy, around 1224, may have been a UFO encounter, and the wounds on his hands, the stigmata, may have been electromagnetic burns: this is a reading Michels returns to again and again, crediting the religious studies scholar Diana Pasulka and her book American Cosmic, and at times the researchers Jacques Vallée and Garry Nolan. He says the earliest accounts, by Francis's friend Brother Leo and the biographer Thomas of Celano, describe not Christ but "atmospheric sparks," "a flaming torch" and a spinning disk, and he adds that Francis died from it a year or two later. Pasulka, telling it herself from the early sources, says Leo, then about 15, saw something come out of the sky with sparks, seemingly spinning, that "dealt harshly with Francis," leaving him injured, though she calls the being a seraph, an angel, and does not herself speak of radiation.
